name: Glutathione
lead: Glutathione is a tripeptide made of glutamate, cysteine and glycine and is the main small-molecule antioxidant inside most cells. It is available as oral, sublingual, topical and intravenous products.

It is heavily marketed, particularly in parts of Asia, for skin lightening, and it is discussed in looksmaxxing forums for the same purpose. Controlled evidence of visible whitening is limited and inconsistent, and professional bodies have warned against intravenous use for this purpose.

paras: Proposed lightening mechanisms include inhibition of tyrosinase, the key melanin-producing enzyme, and a shift from darker eumelanin toward lighter pheomelanin through cysteine availability. Oral glutathione is poorly absorbed and largely broken down in the gut, so it is unclear how much reaches skin melanocytes.

Intravenous use outside medical indications has been linked to rashes and severe allergic or skin reactions, and some regulators, including the Philippine FDA and dermatology societies, have issued warnings. Injectable products from informal sources carry contamination and dosing risks. Any lightening seen in small studies tends to be mild and may reverse after stopping.
